column2: ENGLISH
Call the Winter

Go out onto the snow at midnight and call the deep cold of the north down on the enemies in your lord's lands. Their camps will freeze and their horses will die in the lines. The cold does not always know friend from foe, and the granaries at home may suffer too.
Has at least 300 society currency
Has not called the winter in the last five years
The Tzar's Call

The north is in Kislev. Send envoys to the Emperor and the electors, the Dwarf kings, the King of Bretonnia, the Phoenix King and the princes of Tilea and Estalia, and remind them who has stood between them and the Wastes for a thousand years.
Brothers in the North
Kislev and the Empire have bled together against Chaos for centuries. Offer the Emperor the old treaty: an alliance of the two crowns, to stand together when the north comes south.
Call on Kislev
The Empire is at war with Chaos. Call on the ruler of Kislev to ride south, as the Tzars have before.
The chieftain escapes into the steppe. He will be back.
Kislev Winter
The winter of Kislev has closed on this land. Foreign armies freeze, starve and sicken here.
The Called Winter
An Ice Witch has called the deep cold of the north down on this land. Nothing that marches here will march for long.
Winter Famine
The cold called on the enemy came home too. The granaries are frozen and the people are hungry.
Burned Stanitsa
The Kurgan burned this land in the Spring Driving. Its people are dead, fled or carried off north.
Stanitsa of Heroes
This stanitsa held alone against the hordes of the north. There is a song about it, and every young man of the oblast wants to serve on its walls.
Northern Refugees
Refugees from the burned stanitsas of the north have settled here. They work hard and they remember everything.
The Lynsk Line
The forts along the Lynsk are manned to the last loophole. The river will be held.
Scorched Earth
The land along the Lynsk was burned in the pull-back. Nothing here will feed an army.
Called the Winter
Called the winter on the enemy not long ago.
Frostbitten
Marched through a Kislev winter not long ago.
The Spring Driving
Faced the Spring Driving not long ago.
The Motherland Calls
A Black Crusade has come to Kislev, and every Kislevite knows what that means. Nobody is running, and nobody is rebelling.
The Siege of Praag
Praag was besieged by Chaos not long ago.
The Lynsk Line
Chaos crossed the Lynsk not long ago.
Bleeding on the Lynsk
The forts on the Lynsk are held, but every week the levies send more men to fill them.
A Stanitsa's Last Stand
A northern stanitsa made its last stand not long ago.
Time Bought in Blood
A northern garrison died to buy the realm time. The time has been used.
Warned by the Strigany
The Strigany brought word of the enemy's plans. The realm's armies are ready for him.
The Call Sent
Called the powers of the Old World to war not long ago.
Brothers in the North
Offered the old treaty not long ago.
Shield of the North
Sent Gold for the War
Refused the Call
Brothers in the North
Rode to My Relief
Left My Stanitsa to Fall
Chieftain's Skull-Torc
A heavy torc of black iron hung with the small skulls of a Kurgan chieftain's victims. He led the Spring Driving over the Lynsk for years. Now his own skull is on the end of it.

The witch goes out onto the snow at midnight with her hair unbound. By the time she comes back the stars have gone white. In the morning the rivers in the north are frozen solid and the enemy's horses are dead in their lines, and the cold is still coming.
Let them freeze.

The snow is barely gone from the steppe and they are already over the Lynsk. A rider comes in with his horse half dead: Kurgan, hundreds of them, under a chieftain called [spring_chieftain.GetFirstName], burning their way toward the stanitsas of [spring_province.GetName]. It is the Spring Driving, as it is every year.

The snow is barely gone from the steppe and he is back. [spring_chieftain.GetFirstName], the same chieftain as before, has come over the Lynsk again with his riders, and the smoke is already rising over [spring_province.GetName]. The stanitsa people say he swore to come back every spring until he has your head.
Saddle up. We ride out to meet them.
Man the walls of the stanitsa and hold.
Send gold and let them ride on.

They come down the roads from the north in their hundreds, with carts, cattle and children, and nothing else. The stanitsa is ash. They ask for land and for bread. Some of the boyars say there are already too many mouths to feed this year.
Give them land near the capital.
Turn them away. We cannot feed them.

[spring_chieftain.GetFirstName] came at you through the smoke, roaring, and you cut him down. His riders saw him fall and broke for the river. They will not be back this year. His men will tell the story of it around their fires in the Wastes, and so will yours.
Take the torc. Leave him for the crows.

The Black Crusade has come. The hordes of the Wastes are marching south and Kislev is the first thing in their way, as it always has been. In every stanitsa and every town the priests of Ursun ring the bells, and men who have never touched a lance take one down from the wall. Nobody talks of running. The Motherland calls.
For Kislev.

It is over. The Black Crusade broke on Kislev like a wave on a rock, and what is left of the hordes is limping back north over the Lynsk. Every temple bell in the Tzardom rings for a day and a night. Far to the south, in towns that never saw a Kurgan, people sleep a little easier and never know why.
The wall holds.

A long column of Dwarfs comes down out of the World's Edge, in mail and iron and with guns on their shoulders. Their captain, [karaz_captain.GetFirstName], bows exactly as low as he must and not a hair lower. The Oath of Karaz, he says, was sworn over the passes near Praag in the days of his great-grandfather's grandfather, and the Dwarfs do not forget an oath.
Kislev remembers too. Welcome, friends.

The hordes of Chaos are camped all round Praag, so many fires that the night is red. The boyars on the walls look at you. A sortie out of the north gate could burn their siege engines before they are finished. It could also be the last thing anyone in it ever does.
Open the gate. I lead the sortie.
Keep the walls. Let them come to us.

At dawn the wall by the north gate came down in a cloud of dust, and now the breach is full of screaming things. Someone has to hold it while the masons build a new wall behind. Whoever holds it will not come back.
[praag_hero.GetFirstName] will hold it.
I hold it myself.

[praag_hero.GetFirstName] held the breach for a day and a night. When the new wall behind it was finished, the masons called down to come back, and there was no answer. The bards of Praag are already singing about it.
Praag will remember.

The siege is over. The hordes of Chaos have gone back north, and Praag, which has fallen so many times, still stands. The people come out of the cellars into the light and sing in the streets. This time the city held.
Praag holds.

Riders come in from the Lynsk on blown horses. The hordes are over the river. The forts along the Lynsk can be held, if every levy in the Tzardom sends men to fill them, or the Tzardom can pull back to the cities, burn everything between, and meet the enemy later with a fresh host.
Hold the river. Not one step back.
Pull back to the cities and burn the land behind us.
The levies called in after the pull-back from the Lynsk are mustered at the capital: lancers, horse archers, streltsi and pikes. They are ready to march north.
Then let them march.

A rider from [stand_lord.GetTitledName] got through the lines with one message: the stanitsa in [stand_province.GetName] is surrounded by a whole horde and has a few hundred men on its walls. They will hold as long as they can. Every day they hold, the realm has one more day. Relieving them means riding into the teeth of the horde.
We ride to relieve them.
They will buy us the time we need.
A company of Dwarf rangers comes down out of the mountains, grim and silent, and offers to fight. They have their own grudges against the north.
Welcome, rangers.
A free company of Ostland and Talabecland men has crossed the border to fight. Their captain says the Empire remembers who stands between it and the Wastes, even if its princes do not.
The Empire has not forgotten us.
The Gryphon Legion has come home. Word of the war reached them in the Empire and they rode north without waiting for orders. They want no pay for this one.
The Legion rides with us.

A Bretonnian knight in battered armour rides in from the west, alone. There is a grail on his shield, and something in his eyes that makes the boyars step aside. He has heard there is a war against the Ruinous Powers here, and he asks only to fight in it.
Welcome, Sir Knight.
A coven of Ice Witches comes in from the north and goes out to the enemy's camps at night. In the morning the camps are frozen in, the rivers are ice and the horses are dead in their lines.
The Ice Queen's daughters fight for us.

In the night the bears came out of the forest. Nobody called them. They went through the Chaos camp like a storm, and by dawn there were tents torn open and men lying in the snow. The priests of Ursun say the god himself sent them.
Ursun is with us.

A company of the Knights of the White Star rides in from Erengrad, white wolf pelts over their armour, and offers its lances. They are Ulricans, and the priests of Ursun look sour. The knights do not care.
Lances are lances.
An Elf mage who came on the ships to Erengrad offers to stand with the realm. The enemy will not like what he can do. He has not said why he wants to help, and nobody has asked.
His magic is welcome.

A Strigany woman comes into camp at dusk and asks to see the commander. The enemy will attack tonight, she says, from the woods to the east. She was right. The attack is broken before it begins. The Strigany will expect a favour.
Pay her well.
Tell her Kislev owes her.

An envoy from [From.GetTitledName] stands before you, still in his travelling furs. The hordes of Chaos are in Kislev, he says, and Kislev has stood between you and the Wastes for a thousand years. Now it is asking for help.
We march north. Kislev will not stand alone.
Send a host under one of our captains.
Send gold. It is all we can spare.
We have our own wars.
[From.GetTitledName] has answered the Tzar's Call. Kislev does not stand alone this time.
Good.
An envoy from [From.GetTitledName] offers the old treaty, Brothers in the North: Kislev and the Empire to stand together against the north, as they have for centuries.
Sign it. We are brothers.
The Empire stands alone.
[From.GetTitledName] has sworn the treaty of Brothers in the North. When the north comes south again, Kislev and the Empire will meet it together.
Brothers in the North.
An envoy from [From.GetTitledName] has come. The Empire is fighting the hordes of Chaos, and the Emperor calls on Kislev to ride south as the Tzars have before.
Kislev rides south.
Kislev has its own war to fight.
[From.GetTitledName] is dead, and you killed him. One less champion of the Ruinous Powers walks the world. The priests of Ursun will hear of it before nightfall.
Go back to the Wastes in pieces.
ENGLISH
Has not hired out the Kossars in the last fifteen years
The Kossars ride home at once. The southern prince keeps the rest of the contract money.
The Kossars come home hard and proud, and teach the levies what they learned in the south.
The Kossars come home with southern gold in their saddlebags, and your share of it.
Fewer come home than went. The ones who return tell the story of the ones who did not.
You cut it down, but by morning the body is gone. Trolls heal.

The bear-master leads it out into the courtyard on a chain as thick as a man's wrist: a great bear of the line of Urskin, the bear that Tzar Boris rode against the hordes. It is taller than a horse at the shoulder. It looks at you for a long moment, then lowers its head.
Urskin rides again.

A caravan has come down the High Pass out of the east: two hundred camels and yaks, loaded with jade, silk, spices and ivory from far Cathay. It has crossed the Ogre lands to reach Praag, and the merchants are asking for an escort west. They are also, the tax-farmers point out, very rich.
Give them an escort, for a fee.
Tax them for every bale.
Let them pass freely. Word will spread.
A rider comes in from the Pass, half dead. The caravan was attacked in the high valleys by raiders, some say Ogres and some say greenskins, and the escort is fighting for its life.
Ride to their rescue.
They are already lost.
The merchants of Cathay have long memories. Word of Praag's tolls has gone back along the road, and for years to come the caravans will go round by the south and the Pass will be empty.
Their loss.

The captain of the Kreml Guard kneels before the Ice Throne in full armour, with the whole guard behind him. He swears the old oath in person: to stand between the crown and every knife in the dark, until death or the end of the reign.
I accept your oath.
Swear it again, on Ursun's altar.

The Kossars have come home. Ten years ago they rode south to fight for a foreign prince. Now they ride back through the gates in a long column, burned brown by southern suns, and the whole town turns out to count them.
Welcome home.

A letter has come from the captain of the Kossars you hired out to the south. They have taken a city in Tilea for their prince and held a pass in the Border Princes against greenskins. The prince is slow to pay, the wine is thin, and every man of them misses the snow.
Good. They make Kislev proud.
Longships have been seen off the coast of [north_raided_coast.GetName], a dozen of them with dragon prows and painted shields. By tomorrow the Norscans will be on the beaches.
Meet them on the shore.
Pay them to sail on.
Send Erengrad's ships to catch them at sea.

The raiders are broken and their jarl has been dragged before you in chains, still laughing. He says his people will pay for him, or burn your coast for a hundred years if you kill him. He seems curious which you will choose.
Ransom him to his people.
Bring him before Ursun.
Keep him. His people will keep the peace while he lives.

The thaw has come to the north, and with it the trolls. One has come down from the hills into [north_troll_province.GetName], and the herdsmen say it has eaten forty cattle and two men, and is still hungry.
Hunt it down.
Pay the troll-hunters.
Bar the gates and wait for it to move on.
The troll is back. The one you cut down a year ago has grown back the arm you took and is eating the herds again, and it seems to remember you.
Burn it this time.
Call on the Circle of the Bear.
Urskin's Bear in the Forest
A great bear of Urskin's line roams the forests here. The people say it guards them.
The High Pass Trade
Word has spread that Praag treats the caravans well, and more of them come.
Cathay Shuns the Pass
The merchants of Cathay take the long road round, and the High Pass is empty.
Raided by Norscans
Norscan longships have burned this coast.
A Troll Loose
A troll is eating its way through the herds of this province.
Sworn by the Kreml Guard
The Kreml Guard has sworn to stand between this ruler and every knife in the dark.
Kossars Abroad
A company of Kossars is fighting for a southern prince.
Hired Out the Kossars
Has hired out the Kossars recently.
Kossar Veterans
The Kossars have come home from the south and are teaching the levies.
Norscan Hostage
Holds a Norscan jarl as hostage, and his people leave this coast alone.
Raise a Bear of Urskin's Line
Have the Tzar's bear-master raise a great bear of the line of Urskin, the bear that Tzar Boris rode. One for each Tzar. It dies with its rider, or goes back to the wilds, and never passes to an heir.
Hire Out the Kossars
Hire a company of Kossars out to a southern prince for ten years. Gold now, fewer men at home until they come back.
Recall the Kossars
Chaos has come. Buy out the Kossars' contract and bring them home.
Bear of Urskin's Line
A great bear of the line of Urskin, taller than a horse at the shoulder. It serves one rider, and when he dies it will serve no other.
Troll-Hide Cloak
A cloak of grey-green troll hide that knits itself back together when it is cut.
Builds Tall
Holds the whole of Kislev and guards it.
